rv.q: It’s vividly brought to life by Fionna Hewitt-Twamley, in a virtuoso performance that has rightly won acclaim at the Edinburgh Fringe and elsewhere.
There’s a disarming honesty to this intriguing production, as courageous as it is charming.
Myra’s Story is well-intentioned but its tone is constantly uneven.
Script and performer combine for a fine display of Irish storytelling.

cn.t: Hewitt-Twamley delivers an impassioned performance in this well-intentioned Irish monologue about homelessness and addiction, though critics find Foster's script uneven in tone despite its worthy cause and emotional impact.
